title: Edgecom design handoff manifest
description: The file a Claude Design output ships beside itself — `<Name>.manifest.json` next to `<Name>.dc.html` — naming the design-system version and digest the design was built against and the registry component behind every designed element. It is authored by the design step, not extracted afterwards: a rendered design carries neither. A coding agent reads it to verify the version, resolve each instance to its published contract at https://design.edgecom.ai/contracts/<component>.json, and check that the variants, tokens and states the design relies on exist. Validate with https://design.edgecom.ai/tools/check-design-manifest.mjs.

schemaVersion.description: The manifest format. Bump only when a field changes meaning.

design.description: Path of the design this manifest describes, relative to the design project root — `Settings.dc.html`, `screens/permissions.dc.html`. One manifest per design file.

title.description: What the design is, for a human reading the manifest.

designSystemVersion.description: Copied from the design project's `_system.json` → `designSystemVersion`. Must equal `version` in https://design.edgecom.ai/contracts/index.json for the design to be current.

designSystemDigest.description: Copied from `_system.json` → `designSystemDigest`. The content identity of the whole system — tokens, design language, primitives, authored overlays — and the same value every published artifact carries as `digest`. A different digest means a different system.

designSystemCommit.description: Copied from `_system.json` → `designSystemCommit`. Informational: the digest, not the commit, is the identity.

generatedAt.description: When the manifest was written, ISO 8601.

screens.description: The screens a multi-screen design switches between — the values of its `activeSection` prop, or one entry per view. Instances cite one by `screen`.

components.description: One entry per designed element that is a design-system component. The instance-level form of the screen map: what is on the screen, which registry component it is, and which of that component's variants it uses.

tokens.description: Every semantic token the design reaches for directly — by `var(--x)` or a utility naming it — outside what the components already carry. Ids as in https://design.edgecom.ai/tokens.json (`primary`, not `--primary`).

viewports.description: The viewports the design was drawn for. `mobile` and `desktop` are both required for a design to be complete.

themes.description: The themes the design was checked in. Both are required; every token has both values.

states.description: The states the design shows for the screen as a whole. `loading`, `empty`, `error` and `success` are required for a design to be complete — a screen that only shows the happy path is not implementable.

interactions.description: What happens when: which instance, on which event, produces which result. What an implementing agent otherwise has to infer.

result.description: In words, naming other instances by id where it helps: `opens confirm-remove`.

approvedExceptions.description: Deviations from a contract or from design.md that were approved, and by whom. The only way a deviation is allowed (precedence rule 5); anything not listed here is a defect to report, not a choice to keep.

rule.description: The rule being deviated from, as a contract field or a design.md sentence.

instanceId.description: Unique within the manifest. Put the same value on the element as `data-instance="…"` so the manifest and the markup can be joined.

component.description: The registry component's id, as listed in https://design.edgecom.ai/contracts/index.json — `alert-dialog`, not `AlertDialog`.

label.description: What this instance is on the screen: `Save permissions`, `Members table`.

variants.description: One entry per variant axis the instance sets, keyed by the axis name the contract lists — `variant`, `size`, `orientation`, … — with the chosen option as value. Omitted axes take the contract's default.

parts.description: The parts of a compound component this instance composes, by the names the contract lists — `DialogHeader`, `DialogFooter`.

states.description: States drawn for this instance specifically, where they differ from the screen-level `states`.
